claims.author: A
claims.text: The final Multica dump (TASK-028) is taken after triggers are verified disabled (TASK-027) but while containers still run, yielding an application-consistent snapshot without racing background work.
claims.evidence: TASK-028 'With triggers disabled and containers still running, create a final ... dump'; depends on TASK-027.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Phase 7 correctly closes the autostart gap Migration Assistant leaves: deselecting Applications/System still copies user LaunchAgents, and TASK-039's atomic move plus 'do not log into tetsuo yet' quarantines them before first login.
claims.evidence: TASK-039 moves LaunchAgents to .migrated-disabled and creates empty 0700 dir; TASK-038 'Do not log into tetsuo yet'.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Quarantine tasks are non-destructive (TASK-040/041 'do not delete'), preserving rollback while still preventing autostart.
claims.evidence: TASK-040 'Do not delete it'; TASK-041 'without deleting them'.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Cloud/mail clients can resync between flush (TASK-026) and quit (TASK-031) because TASK-031 depends only on TASK-026 and network stays enabled; add a pre-quit quiescence re-check or disable sync first.
claims.evidence: TASK-031 'wait for cloud clients to finish, then quit'; depends on TASK-026 only; no network-off step.
claims.test: Show whether any monitored client can initiate sync between TASK-026 completion and TASK-031 quit.

claims.author: A
claims.text: TASK-036 implies attempting to automate the security-code/pairing GUI, which is brittle and security-sensitive; it should be unconditionally user-driven.
claims.evidence: 'The user performs only credential/security-code confirmation if GUI automation cannot.'

claims.author: A
claims.text: TASK-033 creates a final Time Machine backup but never verifies restorability, weakening the rollback guarantee the plan otherwise implies.
claims.evidence: 'Run a final Time Machine backup and verify the new snapshot timestamp' — timestamp only, no restore test.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Preconditions TASK-012, TASK-024, TASK-002, and TASK-022 are referenced as dependencies but do not appear in the seed, so their guarantees cannot be verified.
claims.evidence: 'Dependencies: TASK-012, TASK-024'; TASK-037 'unless TASK-022 recorded an approved omission'.

claims.author: A
claims.text: TASK-034 enables FileVault and installs all updates before confirming sufficient free space, but encryption and updates change space and can force reboots; free space should be confirmed first and re-confirmed after updates.
claims.evidence: 'Enable FileVault, install all available macOS updates, restart if required, and confirm sufficient free space' — space confirmed last.

claims.author: B
claims.text: TASK-028 does not establish a write barrier spanning the PostgreSQL dump and uploads archive; server shutdown follows both captures.
claims.test: Inspect server mutation routes and existing worker/request logs for the capture interval. Falsify this concern by demonstrating all scheduled, event-driven, manual/API and in-flight writes are fenced and drained throughout both captures.

history.note: Challenges A1 and A9's sufficiency inference, not the existence of the narrower trigger gate.

claims.author: B
claims.text: TASK-030–031 verify immediate cessation but do not demonstrate persistent restart suppression required by GOAL-005.
claims.test: Read the three scheduled scripts for maintenance-marker guards and inspect existing lifecycle records and persistent-disable evidence for Collie, KSeF and cloud clients. Comprehensive suppression of every applicable relaunch path would falsify the concern.

history.note: A10's long-running Multica persistence is supported; its claim that only Herdr remains exposed is not. No actual restart was attempted.

claims.author: B
claims.text: The destination pre-login gate does not explicitly cover startup mechanisms outside the quarantined user LaunchAgents directory.
claims.test: On the actual destination, inspect sfltool dumpbtm, Login Items and available scheduler records; resolve enabled entries to executables. Demonstrate that no copied runnable writer bypasses quarantine at first login.

history.note: Challenges A2/A3's comprehensive prevention inference. A11 proposes a useful gate but migration of specific registrations remains unverified.

claims.author: A
claims.text: TASK-027 is an explicit write-initiator fence gate ('every registered trigger reports disabled'; 'Do not proceed if any trigger remains enabled') sequenced before TASK-028's dump, so a barrier design is present; B1 conflates unproven factory-stop drain semantics with absence of a barrier.
claims.evidence: TASK-027 verification gate; TASK-028 'with triggers disabled and containers still running' depends on TASK-027.

claims.author: A
claims.text: TASK-029 runs 'multica-ctl freeze -f' to persist disabled overrides and a maintenance marker and verifies labels stopped/disabled and containers down; this is persistent restart suppression for Multica, refuting B2's Multica core. B2 holds only for source-side Herdr (TASK-030 merely preserves plists), which is low-risk since the source is not logged into during transfer.
claims.evidence: TASK-029 'freeze -f to persist disabled overrides and a maintenance marker'; TASK-030 'Preserve their plists and logs' with no persisted disable.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Concede B3: user-scoped Login Items and SMAppService background items (sfltool dumpbtm) plus user cron are migrated inside the tetsuo account but outside ~/Library/LaunchAgents, so TASK-039's quarantine and TASK-042's validation do not cover them. Fix: extend TASK-039/042 to enumerate dumpbtm and Login Items and quarantine/disable before first login. System LaunchDaemons are excluded (System deselected in TASK-037), bounding exposure to user scope.
claims.evidence: TASK-039 moves only LaunchAgents; TASK-042 validates ownership/permissions/checksums, not startup registrations; TASK-037 deselects Applications/System but keeps full user account incl. user Library.
claims.test: On destination as migration-admin, run sfltool dumpbtm and inspect Login Items; resolve enabled entries to executables; confirm none launch pre-login.
